prompt: A buyer and seller exchange enforceable promises to buy and sell a parcel, but no earnest money is required. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Only the seller's deed can supply consideration.
options.explanation: A future conveyance promise can support the bargain before delivery.

options.text: Consideration exists only if price equals appraised value.
options.explanation: Consideration need not equal market value.

options.text: The exchanged promises can supply consideration.
options.explanation: Consideration can consist of promises; a cash deposit is not universally necessary.

options.text: No contract can exist without a 3% deposit.
options.explanation: There is no universal 3% deposit requirement for contract formation.

prompt: A seller signs an offer but changes the closing date as a condition of agreement. The response is ordinarily:

options.text: A rescission of a completed sale.
options.explanation: The facts concern formation, not unwinding an already completed sale.

options.text: A counteroffer requiring the buyer's acceptance.
options.explanation: A qualified acceptance changing a material term proposes a new bargain.

options.text: An unconditional acceptance of the original offer.
options.explanation: The added condition prevents an unconditional matching acceptance.

options.text: A deed transferring title immediately.
options.explanation: A negotiation response does not itself convey the property.

prompt: An agreement has an unlawful object. It is most appropriately classified as:

options.text: Void.
options.explanation: An illegal object prevents the agreement from having ordinary contractual force.

options.text: Fully enforceable if both parties sign.
options.explanation: Signatures do not legalize an unlawful purpose.

options.text: Executed solely because consideration was promised.
options.explanation: Executed performance does not describe this formation defect.

options.text: Automatically valid after notarization.
options.explanation: Acknowledgment does not cure illegality.

prompt: A purchase contract obtained through legally significant fraud may be avoided by the protected party. This illustrates:

options.text: An agreement that no party can ever affirm.
options.explanation: Voidability can allow the protected party to choose affirmation where permitted.

options.text: A contract requiring no consent.
options.explanation: Consent remains essential; the fraud undermines its legal quality.

options.text: A mandatory transfer to the state.
options.explanation: Fraud in formation does not create escheat.

options.text: A voidable agreement.
options.explanation: The protected party can avoid an agreement that otherwise may have effect.

prompt: Which agreement most clearly falls within the real estate lease provision of California's statute of frauds?

options.text: An agreement to water plants tomorrow.
options.explanation: The stated service is not a real property lease.

options.text: A one-day equipment rental solely because rent is charged.
options.explanation: Rent alone does not make a transaction a qualifying real property lease.

options.text: A lease for two years.
options.explanation: A lease longer than one year ordinarily requires a sufficient signed writing.

options.text: A completed two-week vacation rental solely because it involves land.
options.explanation: That duration does not satisfy the longer-than-one-year lease rule.

prompt: An offer expressly requires the buyer to receive signed acceptance by 5 p.m. Friday. The seller signs Friday but delivery occurs Saturday. Which point is decisive?

options.text: The deposit amount extends the deadline automatically.
options.explanation: A deposit does not silently amend the specified acceptance deadline.

options.text: The stated receipt requirement was not met.
options.explanation: The offer's required acceptance method and deadline govern the stated facts.

options.text: The seller's private signature always binds the buyer immediately.
options.explanation: Signing alone does not satisfy an express delivery-and-receipt condition.

options.text: Any acceptance within three days is automatically timely.
options.explanation: There is no universal three-day grace period for accepting offers.

prompt: A signed purchase agreement still requires financing approval, payment, and delivery of title. In the performance sense, it is:

options.text: Executory.
options.explanation: Material contractual duties remain to be performed.

options.text: Fully executed.
options.explanation: Signing does not mean all performance is complete.

options.text: Void for lacking immediate title transfer.
options.explanation: Purchase agreements can validly require later performance.

options.text: An oral agreement.
options.explanation: The facts expressly describe a signed agreement.

prompt: A buyer assigns a purchase contract to another buyer. The seller has not agreed to release the original buyer. Which statement is best?

options.text: The original buyer is always released immediately.
options.explanation: Release ordinarily requires agreement or another legal basis.

options.text: The seller has automatically agreed to a novation.
options.explanation: Assignment alone does not establish consent to substitution and discharge.

options.text: Assignment automatically cancels the purchase contract.
options.explanation: A permitted assignment can continue the agreement with transferred rights.

options.text: The original buyer may remain liable for performance.
options.explanation: Assignment or delegation does not automatically discharge the original obligor.

prompt: All necessary parties agree to substitute a new buyer and discharge the original buyer's obligation. This is:

options.text: An acknowledgment of a deed signature.
options.explanation: Notarial acknowledgment serves a different purpose.

options.text: A subordination agreement.
options.explanation: Subordination changes priority rather than substitutes and releases an obligor.

options.text: A novation.
options.explanation: The agreed substitution includes discharge of the replaced obligation.

options.text: Only a unilateral assignment.
options.explanation: The express release and consent distinguish novation.

prompt: A buyer properly cancels under an unremoved inspection contingency according to the contract. The cancellation is:

options.text: Effective only if the property has already transferred.
options.explanation: Contingencies normally operate before completing the transfer.

options.text: Not necessarily a breach because the contract provides that right.
options.explanation: A valid exercise of an agreed contingency must be distinguished from default.

options.text: Automatically a breach because the buyer signed the offer.
options.explanation: A signed contract can include enforceable cancellation rights.

options.text: Always subject to automatic loss of 3% of the price.
options.explanation: The 3% liquidated-damages rules do not erase contingency rights.

prompt: A court orders a seller to convey land under an enforceable purchase agreement. The remedy is:

options.text: Specific performance.
options.explanation: The order requires the promised act rather than merely paying money.

options.text: Liquidated damages.
options.explanation: Liquidated damages involve an agreed damages measure, not an order to convey.

options.text: Rescission.
options.explanation: Rescission unwinds the agreement rather than compels its performance.

options.text: Mediation.
options.explanation: A mediator ordinarily helps negotiate rather than imposes this order.

prompt: A qualifying owner-occupied residential sale is priced at $900,000. What is 3% of that price for the statutory liquidated-damages analysis?

options.explanation: That is 1%, not 3%, of the purchase price.
That is 3% of $1 million, a different price.
That is 30%, a decimal-place error.
Multiplying $900,000 by 0.03 yields $27,000; other statutory requirements still apply.

prompt: A qualifying residential contract includes a liquidated-damages provision and a deposit below 3%. The buyer and seller dispute whether the buyer defaulted. Escrow should:

options.text: Automatically pay the broker's commission from the deposit.
options.explanation: The disputed trust funds do not automatically belong to the broker.

options.text: Divide the deposit equally without consent.
options.explanation: Escrow cannot invent a settlement allocation.

options.text: Follow authorized instructions and applicable dispute procedures rather than decide default itself.
options.explanation: A liquidated-damages clause does not turn escrow into the adjudicator of disputed rights.

options.text: Automatically give the seller the deposit.
options.explanation: The clause alone does not resolve the disputed default.

prompt: The parties agree to unwind their purchase contract and restore exchanged benefits. This most closely describes:

options.text: A novation continuing the same sale with a new buyer.
options.explanation: No substituted buyer or continuing obligation is described.

options.text: Rescission with restitution.
options.explanation: Rescission unwinds the contract, and restitution addresses returning benefits.

options.text: Specific performance.
options.explanation: Specific performance requires completion rather than unwinding.

options.text: An offer that was never accepted.
options.explanation: The parties are ending an existing agreement.

prompt: Under an exclusive right to sell listing with no applicable exception, the owner personally finds the buyer during the term. The agreed listing compensation is generally:

options.text: Still governed by the exclusive right to sell fee provision.
options.explanation: That listing ordinarily covers sales during the term regardless of who produces the buyer.

options.text: Automatically waived whenever the owner finds the buyer.
options.explanation: That resembles an exclusive-agency owner-sale exception, not the stated listing.

options.text: Fixed by DRE at a statutory percentage.
options.explanation: No statutory commission percentage applies.

options.text: Paid only if the buyer separately hired the listing broker.
options.explanation: The seller's listing obligation does not require that separate relationship.

prompt: Which feature most distinguishes an exclusive agency listing from an exclusive right to sell listing?

options.text: Only an exclusive agency listing must identify a property.
options.explanation: Both must adequately identify their subject and scope.

options.text: An exclusive right to sell automatically conveys title.
options.explanation: Neither listing is a deed.

options.text: An exclusive agency permits competing brokers to hold identical exclusive listings.
options.explanation: It grants exclusivity to one brokerage, subject to the owner's reserved right.

options.text: An owner's independent-sale exception ordinarily exists in the exclusive agency listing.
options.explanation: The distinction concerns the owner's ability to produce the buyer without owing listing compensation.

prompt: Under California regulations operative January 1, 2026, what is the ordinary maximum term represented by three months for a covered individual buyer agreement?

options.text: One year unless the buyer objects.
options.explanation: That exceeds the applicable maximum.

options.text: An unlimited term with automatic monthly renewal.
options.explanation: Covered agreements cannot renew automatically.

options.text: 90 calendar days, with counting governed by the regulation and any agreed delayed effective date.
options.explanation: The regulation defines the statutory term as 90 calendar days.

options.text: Exactly 90 business days.
options.explanation: The rule uses calendar days, not business days.

prompt: For a buyer's agent preparing an in-person property showing in 2026, the DRE timing regulation creates:

options.text: A requirement only for buyers using FHA loans.
options.explanation: The rule is not limited to a particular loan program.

options.text: A rebuttable presumption that obtaining the signed buyer agreement before showing is practicable.
options.explanation: The regulation addresses what is practicable before in-person and defined virtual showings.

options.text: An exception allowing every agreement to wait until closing.
options.explanation: The statute requires execution much earlier, and the regulation addresses showings.

options.text: A rule that every open-house visitor is automatically represented.
options.explanation: A seller-only agent's showing does not itself establish buyer representation.

prompt: A covered buyer representation agreement is approaching expiration. The parties wish to renew. Which method complies with the stated renewal rules?

options.text: A written, dated renewal signed by the parties before expiration within the applicable term limit.
options.explanation: The current rules require affirmative written renewal and prohibit automatic renewal.

options.text: An automatic extension printed in the original agreement.
options.explanation: Automatic renewal is prohibited.

options.text: The broker silently continues the agreement for a year.
options.explanation: Silence does not satisfy the signing or duration requirements.

options.text: An undated oral understanding recorded only in the agent's notes.
options.explanation: The renewal must be written, dated, and signed by the parties.

prompt: A broker plans to collect a regulated advance fee for future marketing services. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The broker may collect immediately upon mailing materials to DRE.
options.explanation: The required prior review and no-objection process must be completed.

options.text: Calling the fee nonrefundable eliminates trust obligations.
options.explanation: The label does not override refundable unexpended funds and accounting requirements.

options.text: Only the salesperson must approve the agreement.
options.explanation: DRE review and broker responsibilities are not replaced by salesperson approval.

options.text: The required materials must be submitted in advance and DRE's no-objection communication received before use or collection.
options.explanation: Submission alone does not authorize immediate use, and DRE does not endorse the services.

prompt: A broker offers to collect an advance fee for covered residential mortgage loan modification services. A general advance-fee agreement:

options.text: Makes the fee lawful if the borrower is late on payments.
options.explanation: Financial distress does not create the claimed exception.

options.text: Eliminates the prohibition after notarization.
options.explanation: Notarial acknowledgment does not change the substantive rule.

options.text: Does not override the prohibition on those advance fees.
options.explanation: The service-specific prohibition controls even if a general form is available.

options.text: Automatically makes the fee lawful.
options.explanation: A contract cannot legalize a prohibited charge.

prompt: A buyer pays for a valid option to purchase by a stated deadline. Before exercising, the buyer ordinarily has:

options.text: A right to change the price unilaterally.
options.explanation: Exercise must comply with the agreed terms.

options.text: The right, but not the obligation, to buy on the option terms.
options.explanation: The optionee has a choice while the optionor's commitment is binding under the option.

options.text: An unconditional duty to buy regardless of exercise.
options.explanation: That confuses an option with an already binding purchase obligation.

options.text: Ownership of the fee immediately.
options.explanation: An unexercised option does not itself complete the conveyance.

prompt: A right of first refusal generally differs from a purchase option because it:

options.text: Typically depends on a sale-related trigger specified in the agreement.
options.explanation: The holder's opportunity commonly arises when the owner decides to sell or receives a qualifying offer.

options.text: Always transfers title when signed.
options.explanation: Neither label alone describes an immediate deed conveyance.

options.text: Always allows an immediate forced sale at any chosen price.
options.explanation: That is not the ordinary first-refusal right.

options.text: Can never appear in a lease.
options.explanation: Lease agreements can contain purchase-related rights.

prompt: Which instrument primarily evidences the borrower's promise to repay money?

options.text: A grant deed from the seller.
options.explanation: The grant deed conveys an ownership interest.

options.text: A preliminary title report.
options.explanation: The report proposes title-insurance terms.

options.text: A lease.
options.explanation: The lease principally grants possession under rental terms.

options.text: A promissory note.
options.explanation: The note states the debt obligation and its payment terms.

prompt: A tenant receives a fixed six-month lease. The duration most clearly creates:

options.text: A mandatory periodic tenancy.
options.explanation: A fixed expiration differs from automatically recurring periods.

options.text: An easement by prescription.
options.explanation: The tenant's possession comes from a lease, not adverse use.

options.text: An estate for years.
options.explanation: A fixed term is an estate for years even when shorter than one year.

options.text: A fee simple estate.
options.explanation: A leasehold does not convey the owner's fee.

prompt: A seller finances a purchase using a land sale contract and retains legal title until required installments are paid. The buyer generally holds:

options.text: Only a right of first refusal.
options.explanation: The buyer has agreed to purchase, not merely to receive a future opportunity.

options.text: An equitable interest under the contract.
options.explanation: The buyer's contractual interest differs from the seller's retained legal title.

options.text: No enforceable interest until the final payment in every case.
options.explanation: The contract can create significant equitable rights before final payment.

options.text: The lender's beneficial interest under an already recorded deed of trust automatically.
options.explanation: The stated arrangement is a land sale contract, not necessarily deed-of-trust financing.

prompt: A lease option credits a $4,000 option payment plus $250 from each of twelve timely rent payments toward the price at a completed purchase. What is the stated credit?

options.explanation: Twelve times $250 is $3,000; adding the $4,000 option credit gives $7,000.
That omits the option payment expressly credited.
That counts only one monthly credit.

options.text: The entire year's rent regardless of the clause.
options.explanation: Only the specified portion of rent receives the contractual credit.

prompt: A buyer offers $620,000. The seller counters at $635,000, and the buyer rejects that counteroffer. The seller then announces acceptance of the original $620,000 offer, which was never renewed. What is the best analysis?

options.text: A contract arose at $620,000 because the buyer initially demonstrated willingness to pay that amount.
options.explanation: The buyer's original willingness does not make a displaced offer continuously available despite intervening rejection.

options.text: The counteroffer displaced the original offer; the seller's later statement does not automatically revive it.
options.explanation: After rejection by counteroffer, the original proposal ordinarily requires renewal or new assent rather than unilateral revival.

options.text: The original offer automatically revives whenever the counteroffer is rejected.
options.explanation: Rejection of a counteroffer does not ordinarily restore a previously rejected original offer.

options.text: A contract arose at $635,000 when the seller signed the counteroffer.
options.explanation: A counteroffer requires acceptance; the stated facts say the buyer rejected it.

prompt: A seller receives a buyer's offer and asks, 'Would you consider a shorter closing?' The seller does not reject the offer or condition acceptance on the change. What distinction matters most?

options.text: Every question about a term rejects the offer even without an expressed condition.
options.explanation: An inquiry and a counteroffer must be distinguished rather than treating all negotiation language identically.

options.text: The requested shorter closing automatically becomes part of the buyer's offer unless the buyer objects.
options.explanation: A proposed possibility does not unilaterally amend the other party's terms.

options.text: An inquiry about possible terms is not necessarily a rejecting counteroffer.
options.explanation: The legal effect depends on what was communicated; asking about flexibility differs from insisting on a substitute bargain.

options.text: The question constitutes unconditional acceptance because no price change was requested.
options.explanation: The seller has not necessarily accepted anything merely by asking about timing.

prompt: An individual negotiates to purchase for an LLC. The draft names the individual as buyer, but the signature is intended to be on the LLC's behalf. What should the agent resolve before execution?

options.text: The identity of the contracting buyer, the signature capacity, and authority to bind that buyer.
options.explanation: Party identification and representative authority should agree; they affect whose obligations the contract creates.

options.text: Only whether the individual owns a majority of the LLC.
options.explanation: Ownership percentage alone does not establish that the draft identifies the intended buyer or that the signer has the needed authority.

options.text: Only whether the LLC's name appears somewhere in the agent's transaction notes.
options.explanation: Private notes do not necessarily resolve a mismatch in the actual agreement and signature capacity.

options.text: Nothing, because every contract negotiated by an LLC member automatically binds the LLC instead of the member.
options.explanation: Entity membership does not automatically correct party identification or establish authority for every transaction.

prompt: A signed purchase agreement contains an integration clause. The buyer later alleges a legally significant fraudulent statement that induced the purchase. What is the soundest conclusion from the clause alone?

options.text: The clause makes all outside statements enforceable as additional contractual promises.
options.explanation: Integration generally addresses the scope of the agreement; it does not automatically incorporate all prior statements.

options.text: The clause conclusively establishes that no statement outside the document could have affected consent.
options.explanation: A statement about the integrated writing does not necessarily resolve every question about how consent was obtained.

options.text: The clause matters to interpretation, but it does not automatically eliminate every fraud claim.
options.explanation: Read the entire agreement and applicable law; an integration clause is not a blanket license for fraudulent inducement.

options.text: The clause automatically makes the written agreement void rather than voidable.
options.explanation: An integration clause does not itself invalidate the agreement; defects in consent require their own analysis.

prompt: A $750,000 purchase anticipates a loan equal to 80% of the price. The lender instead offers 80% of a $700,000 appraisal. The contract has separate appraisal and financing contingencies. What should the buyer's agent identify?

options.text: A $50,000 cash gap and an automatic right to cancel regardless of contingency status.
options.explanation: The price-appraisal difference is $50,000, but the loan shortfall is $40,000; cancellation is not automatic from the arithmetic alone.

options.text: A $150,000 cash gap because the original down payment is the amount missing.
options.explanation: The original down payment was already expected; the new issue is the additional $40,000 caused by the reduced loan.

options.text: No cash gap because the lender is still offering the same 80% percentage.
options.explanation: The percentage is applied to a lower base, so the dollar amount available changes.

options.text: A $40,000 additional cash gap and the distinct requirements of each contingency.
options.explanation: The expected loan is $600,000 and the offered loan is $560,000; cancellation or other rights depend separately on the contract's contingencies.

prompt: The parties sign an amendment extending closing by seven days. It does not change the earlier deposit deadline or any other term. What is the safest contractual reading?

options.text: Every performance deadline automatically shifts seven days because closing controls the entire schedule.
options.explanation: Deadlines may be separately fixed, so an extension of one does not necessarily alter all others.

options.text: The buyer may postpone the deposit until closing because a later amendment outranks all earlier provisions.
options.explanation: A later amendment controls inconsistent provisions within its scope; silence does not necessarily create an inconsistency.

options.text: The original agreement is automatically rescinded and replaced by a wholly new contract.
options.explanation: A limited amendment does not necessarily unwind the entire transaction or discharge unchanged terms.

options.text: The closing date changes; the deposit deadline remains unchanged unless the documents or applicable law establish otherwise.
options.explanation: An amendment should be read for what it actually modifies, not as a blanket extension of every related obligation.

prompt: Buyer and seller sign escrow instructions splitting a disputed $15,000 deposit. The instructions contain no broader release. The seller says this necessarily waives every unrelated contractual claim. What is the best response?

options.text: Escrow decides which remaining claims are waived whenever the instructions omit that issue.
options.explanation: Escrow's limited role does not confer authority to determine the parties' broader disputed contractual rights.

options.text: Neither party can ever release contract claims until a court enters judgment.
options.explanation: Parties can agree to releases without litigation, but the agreement must actually address the rights being relinquished.

options.text: Any instruction distributing earnest money conclusively releases all known and unknown claims.
options.explanation: Distribution alone does not establish the scope of a release, particularly for unrelated or unknown matters.

options.text: The disposition of the deposit and the scope of any release are separate questions.
options.explanation: Instructions can settle custody or allocation of funds without necessarily releasing every substantive claim; examine the actual language and applicable law.

prompt: A qualifying sale of an existing detached home intended for buyer occupancy is priced at $1,000,000. The proposed liquidated damages are the $35,000 actually paid as a deposit. Assuming the statutory requirements otherwise apply, what changes because the amount exceeds 3%?

options.text: Exactly $30,000 must be released to the seller immediately, even if default is disputed.
options.explanation: The threshold is not a direction to escrow to decide default or disburse disputed funds.

options.text: The entire $35,000 is automatically enforceable because the buyer paid it voluntarily.
options.explanation: Payment alone does not resolve the statutory reasonableness analysis or other requirements.

options.text: The party seeking enforcement must establish that the amount is reasonable under the statutory framework.
options.explanation: The amount exceeds the $30,000 threshold; above that level the relevant statutory burden differs rather than the entire sum automatically becoming valid.

options.text: The provision is automatically enforceable for $5,000 because only the amount above the threshold counts.
options.explanation: The excess is not the only amount subject to the provision; this subtraction misunderstands the threshold's function.

prompt: An individual buyer and broker complete the last signature on September 10, 2026, with no delayed effective date. What is the 90th calendar day under the ordinary maximum-term counting rule?

options.text: December 8, 2026.
options.explanation: This incorrectly counts the last-signature date as day one instead of beginning on the following day.

options.text: December 31, 2026.
options.explanation: The agreement does not run automatically through the end of the third later calendar month.

options.text: December 9, 2026.
options.explanation: Counting begins September 11: 20 September days plus 31 October days plus 30 November days equals 81, followed by nine December days.

options.text: December 10, 2026.
options.explanation: Three named calendar months is not the regulation's 90-calendar-day calculation in these circumstances.

prompt: An individual purchases rentals in the individual's own name and requests a six-month buyer representation agreement, claiming to be an investment business. Which statement is best?

options.text: Investment use alone does not qualify the individual for the corporation, LLC, or partnership maximum-term exception.
options.explanation: The exception depends on the actual contracting entity, not simply the economic purpose of an individual's purchase.

options.text: Any income-producing purchase qualifies for the entity exception regardless of the buyer's legal identity.
options.explanation: Investment purpose and entity status are separate facts; one does not substitute for the other.

options.text: The 24-month residential listing limit controls because the purchase concerns a residential rental.
options.explanation: Seller listing duration rules and buyer representation duration rules govern different agreements.

options.text: A six-month term is valid whenever the buyer, rather than the broker, proposes it.
options.explanation: The source of the request does not override the applicable statutory duration limit.

prompt: An individual owner signs a new exclusive listing for a covered California single-family residence with a 36-month initial term. No entity exception applies. Which rule addresses the defect?

options.text: The listing is valid because only renewals, not initial terms, have a maximum duration.
options.explanation: The Act regulates both ordinary initial terms and renewals, with different maximums.

options.text: The Residential Exclusive Listing Agreements Act generally caps that initial term at 24 months.
options.explanation: The covered residential listing exceeds the ordinary initial limit; these listing restrictions are distinct from buyer-agreement rules.

options.text: The listing becomes enforceable if the broker records a memorandum giving public notice.
options.explanation: The Act prohibits recording the listing or a memorandum or notice; recording is not a cure for an impermissible term.

options.text: The buyer representation rule caps the seller's listing at 90 days.
options.explanation: The 90-day maximum concerns covered buyer agreements, not this seller's exclusive listing.

prompt: A broker receives a regulated $2,000 advance fee. Before cancellation, only $600 is properly expended for the specified services, and no other earned or permitted charges apply. What is the unexpended refundable amount?

options.text: $2,000, because advance fees can never be applied to services that were actually performed.
options.explanation: Proper expenditures for the specified services matter; the entire advance is not necessarily unexpended.

options.text: $1,400, supported by the required accounting of the $600 expenditure.
options.explanation: Subtract properly expended funds from the advance; the unused balance remains subject to refund and accounting requirements.

options.text: $600, because that is the amount of performance completed before cancellation.
options.explanation: This reverses the analysis by refunding the expended portion instead of the remaining balance.

options.text: $0, if the agreement labels the payment a nonrefundable marketing package.
options.explanation: A label cannot remove the governing trust, refund, and verified-accounting protections.

prompt: A $640,000 purchase uses a $16,000 deposit already paid and a $496,000 loan. Buyer closing costs are $12,000, offset by a permitted $5,000 seller credit. How much additional buyer cash is needed?

options.explanation: This adds the seller credit as an expense instead of subtracting it from the buyer's cash requirement.
Compute $640,000 minus $16,000 minus $496,000 plus $12,000 minus $5,000.
This fails to credit the $16,000 deposit already supplied by the buyer.
This covers the price balance but omits the net $7,000 in buyer closing costs.

prompt: An option permits purchase for $520,000 through a stated deadline. Before that deadline, the optionee sends a notice saying, 'I exercise only if you reduce the price to $510,000.' The owner does not agree. What is the best characterization?

options.text: A conditional proposal that does not match the option's exercise terms.
options.explanation: An option must be exercised according to its terms; conditioning acceptance on a new price is not an unqualified exercise.

options.text: A valid exercise at $520,000 because the word exercise appears in the notice.
options.explanation: The express condition prevents treating the statement as unconditional assent to the existing bargain.

options.text: A valid exercise at $510,000 because the notice was timely.
options.explanation: Timeliness does not authorize the optionee to alter the fixed price unilaterally.

options.text: An automatic extension of the option while the owner considers the requested reduction.
options.explanation: A conditional proposal does not automatically extend the option deadline.

prompt: A tenant has three years remaining on a lease and transfers possession for two years while retaining the final year, subject to applicable lease restrictions. This retained portion of the term most directly supports which classification?

options.text: An assignment solely because the new occupant receives exclusive possession during the two years.
options.explanation: Exclusive possession during a shorter period does not eliminate the original tenant's retained reversion in the leasehold.

options.text: A sale of the landlord's fee interest because the new occupant pays the original tenant.
options.explanation: Payment to a tenant for possession does not convey ownership the tenant does not hold.

options.text: A novation that automatically releases the original tenant from the landlord's contract.
options.explanation: A substitute occupant does not automatically create the landlord's agreement to discharge the original tenant.

options.text: A sublease rather than a transfer of the entire remaining leasehold.
options.explanation: The tenant retains part of the existing term, distinguishing the arrangement from an assignment of the entire remainder.

prompt: A written repayment promise expressly makes payment dependent on a development project's profits. Which distinction should the agent recognize?

options.text: The condition can affect negotiability without necessarily making every contractual promise unenforceable.
options.explanation: Negotiable-instrument requirements and general contract enforceability are different analyses; a conditional promise needs examination under both as relevant.

options.text: A note that is not negotiable can never support any contractual obligation.
options.explanation: Failure to qualify as a negotiable instrument does not itself eliminate ordinary contract rights.

options.text: Every signed repayment promise is negotiable regardless of express conditions.
options.explanation: Negotiability has substantive requirements; a signature alone does not satisfy them.

options.text: Recording a deed of trust automatically removes the condition from the repayment promise.
options.explanation: Security for an obligation does not rewrite the underlying note's payment terms.

prompt: An ordinary revocable offer expressly requires the buyer's receipt of signed acceptance. The seller signs Thursday. Before delivery, the seller receives the buyer's effective withdrawal at noon Friday. The signed acceptance reaches the buyer at 2 p.m., before the original 5 p.m. deadline. What controls?

options.text: Thursday's signature necessarily controls even though the offer expressly requires receipt.
options.explanation: This disregards the specified method for effective acceptance.

options.text: Receipt before 5 p.m. necessarily creates a contract regardless of the noon withdrawal.
options.explanation: Timely receipt does not revive an offer already effectively withdrawn under the stipulated facts.

options.text: The prescribed acceptance event occurred after effective withdrawal, so meeting the original deadline alone did not form the contract.
options.explanation: The offer had to remain open when the required receipt occurred; the earlier signature does not satisfy the express receipt condition.

options.text: The stated Friday deadline necessarily made the offer irrevocable until 5 p.m.
options.explanation: An ordinary offer's expiration does not itself create a binding option or another restriction on revocation.

prompt: An offer requires receipt of the seller's signed unchanged acceptance. The buyer receives it at 11 a.m. At noon the seller receives the buyer's attempted withdrawal. Assuming all formation requirements are satisfied, what is the buyer's next legal question?

options.text: Whether a contractual cancellation right, mutual agreement, or other applicable remedy permits ending the formed contract.
options.explanation: The attempt follows effective acceptance; the problem has moved from revocation of an offer to rights under an existing contract.

options.text: Whether the noon withdrawal automatically revokes the already accepted offer.
options.explanation: An effective acceptance ordinarily ends the ability to withdraw using the preformation revocation rule.

options.text: Whether the original offer deadline preserves revocation rights even after effective acceptance.
options.explanation: The outside acceptance deadline does not ordinarily preserve a power to revoke once the offer has been effectively accepted.

options.text: Whether the absence of a completed escrow means the agreement is still only a revocable offer.
options.explanation: An executory contract can be binding before escrow closes; incomplete performance is not the same as incomplete formation.

prompt: A party has valid grounds to rescind a completed purchase and has received benefits under it. Subject to section 1691's applicable qualifications, which proposal best fits the ordinary restoration requirement?

options.text: Keep all received benefits permanently while demanding unconditional return of every payment.
options.explanation: That proposal is inconsistent with ordinary unwinding and restoration absent a relevant exception.

options.text: Return benefits only after collecting punitive damages, regardless of the governing claim.
options.explanation: A demand for a separate remedy does not replace the stated restoration requirement.

options.text: Treat delivery of any preclosing inspection form as automatic restoration of completed-sale benefits.
options.explanation: A form label does not perform the restoration or supply the proper postclosing rescission process.

options.text: Offer to restore the received benefits on condition that the other party likewise restores what it received.
options.explanation: The statute permits an appropriate reciprocal restoration offer; actual facts and statutory qualifications still govern.

prompt: A buyer with an alleged postclosing fraud claim wants to keep the property while obtaining compensation for provable loss. The buyer calls this rescission. Which distinction is most important?

options.text: Every claim based on fraud necessarily requires surrender of the property before any remedy can be evaluated.
options.explanation: The asserted misconduct does not automatically make rescission the only possible remedy.

options.text: Keeping the property while seeking compensation calls for a separate damages analysis rather than assuming the sale has been unwound.
options.explanation: Remedies have different objectives and requirements; rescission ordinarily seeks restoration rather than retention of the entire bargain.

options.text: Calling the demand rescission automatically transfers title back even while the buyer insists on ownership.
options.explanation: A chosen label does not itself reverse a conveyance or resolve restoration requirements.

options.text: A buyer who retains property can never assert any claim related to its purchase.
options.explanation: Retention does not categorically eliminate every possible damages claim; the facts and governing law control.

prompt: An individual buyer agreement is last signed September 10, 2026, but expressly sets September 15 as the delayed effective date for its maximum ninety-day initial term. Which date is day ninety?

options.text: December 13, 2026.
options.explanation: Count September 15 as day one: 16 September days plus 31 October days plus 30 November days plus 13 December days equals 90.

options.text: December 9, 2026.
options.explanation: That uses the ordinary day-after-signature start and ignores the expressly agreed delayed starting date.

options.text: December 14, 2026.
options.explanation: That delays counting until the day after the agreed delayed effective date rather than using that date as the start.

options.text: December 15, 2026.
options.explanation: That treats the limit as three calendar months rather than the regulatory ninety calendar days.

prompt: A covered individual buyer agreement expires December 13. Both parties sign an otherwise compliant written renewal on December 1. Under the DRE renewal rule, when does the renewal become effective?

options.text: December 14, automatically following expiration of the original term.
options.explanation: That is not the regulation's stated effective-date rule for the signed renewal.

options.text: December 2, because every renewal uses the initial agreement's day-after-signature rule.
options.explanation: The renewal provision expressly specifies the day of the last signature.

options.text: Only when the buyer makes another offer, because signing renewals does not establish an effective date.
options.explanation: A new purchase offer is not the specified trigger for renewal effectiveness.

options.text: December 1, the day the last party signs the renewal.
options.explanation: The regulation identifies the renewal's last-signature date; it does not automatically stack the new period after prior expiration.

prompt: An otherwise qualifying note unconditionally promises a fixed $100,000 principal amount and describes interest using a variable index-based rate. Does the variable rate alone defeat negotiability?

options.text: Yes; both principal and every future interest amount must be fixed numerically when signed.
options.explanation: The statute permits variable interest descriptions and references to outside information.

options.text: No; Commercial Code section 3112 permits variable interest, distinct from a condition on whether repayment is owed.
options.explanation: The fixed-principal and unconditional-payment requirements should not be confused with a requirement that every interest rate remain constant.

options.text: Yes, unless a deed of trust is recorded, because recording makes the interest rate fixed.
options.explanation: Recording security does not convert a variable rate into a fixed rate or provide the stated exception.

options.text: No, because any document secured by real estate is automatically negotiable.
options.explanation: The answer cannot rest on collateral; all relevant negotiable-instrument requirements still must be met.

prompt: A real estate licensee markets investment notes secured by deeds of trust and says collateral eliminates the need to examine securities registration or licensing. What is the soundest evaluation?

options.text: Recording each deed of trust automatically constitutes SEC approval of the investment.
options.explanation: County recording does not supply federal securities approval.

options.text: Securities rules apply only if the property securing the notes is outside California.
options.explanation: Collateral location does not supply that blanket exemption.

options.text: Secured promissory notes can raise securities requirements independently of the real estate collateral and license.
options.explanation: The offering's substance and applicable registration, exemption, and licensing rules require separate review.

options.text: A note's negotiability conclusively determines whether securities regulation applies.
options.explanation: Negotiable-instrument classification and securities treatment are separate legal analyses.
